threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can always tell the newcomers; they still think Dalston's just a place with cafes, not an underground music hub where every night is a surprise.
Last night on the 59, a guy serenaded the whole bus with 90s R&B. Only in Brixton would people actually join in instead of shushing him.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Walking past the bakery on Weserstraße and catching the scent of fresh bread mixed with the sound of a street musician playing an old folk tune. That's when it hit me.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you see guys setting up a full bar on the sidewalk for a spontaneous party, complete with disco lights and homemade cocktails.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their reaction to BART delays; the eye roll is universal. Newcomers still look at their phones like there's a solution.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Last week, a Muni bus driver calmly pulled over mid-route to help a lost tourist read the map. Classic SF kindness in the chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the Sagrada Família is the heart of Barcelona. Try finding a local in Gràcia who doesn't prefer a pint on a quiet terrace instead.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always spot a recent arrival by their confusion when the metro goes on strike, checking their phones for train times like it’s a lifeline.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still ask for directions to the nearest tube and avoid the number 38 bus like it's the plague. Just wait till you know the shortcuts.
Caught the N37 last night, and the driver was belting out 90s R&B like it was karaoke. Gave everyone a laugh while we crawled past the closed pubs.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The smell of fresh kebab merging with the sound of a street artist playing jazz on Karl-Marx-Straße had me hooked—pure Neukölln magic.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can spot spontaneous dance parties in the middle of the street, especially when the weather’s nice. It’s like a flash mob, but Berlin just calls it Tuesday.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell who's local by their reaction to the Muni delays; real ones just roll their eyes and keep scrolling their phones.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today that had a guy playing a saxophone, while another passenger was trying to sell homemade bracelets. Only in the Tenderloin.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think Gràcia is all about trendy bars, but they miss the small bakeries that open at dawn, where the real local mornings start.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by how they awkwardly navigate the bus system, clutching their T10 card like a lifeline while staring at Google Maps.
